preview_description: UX/UI design for websites, client portals and mobile apps: from a Figma prototype to developer-ready designs.
title: UX/UI design for websites, interfaces and mobile apps
introtext: I design interfaces people don't have to figure out: company websites, client portals, mobile apps. I'm a developer too, so my designs stay realistic — no ideas that look great in Figma and fall apart in code.

tasks.title: What clients come to me with

items.title: A new website or product
items.text: Structure, user flows and look need to be thought through from scratch. We start with a prototype, not with pretty pictures.

items.title: A redesign
items.text: The website looks dated, doesn't reflect the brand, or confuses people. That's how the new Benefit Litigation website came about — after several law firms merged.

items.title: A complex interface
items.text: A client portal, a dashboard or an app with dozens of screens. Here logic matters more than visual effects.

items.title: A UX audit
items.text: The website exists, but leads are few or users complain. I find where people stumble and give you a prioritised list of fixes.

blocks.title: Research
blocks.content: I look into the business goal, the audience and the competition. If there's analytics, I check where people drop off and what they search for.

blocks.title: Prototype
blocks.content: Structure and user flows as a clickable Figma prototype. Changes here are cheap: we move blocks around instead of redrawing designs.

blocks.title: Visual design
blocks.content: Style, typography, colour, illustration and motion. Versions for phone, tablet and desktop.

blocks.title: Design system
blocks.content: Buttons, fields, cards, spacing and colours collected into a component library. New pages are assembled from ready-made parts, and the product looks consistent.

blocks.title: Mobile apps
blocks.content: Interfaces for iOS and Android that follow platform guidelines: navigation, gestures, system components, dark mode.

blocks.title: Developer handoff
blocks.content: Designs with every state, responsive rules and exported assets. If I'm also building it, nothing gets lost along the way.

blocks.title: Meaning before style
blocks.content: Every screen answers one question: what should a person do here? If there's no answer, the screen isn't needed.

blocks.title: Less, but more precise
blocks.content: I turn a complex process into a few clear steps. Every element on screen serves the task instead of filling space.

blocks.title: Design that can be built
blocks.content: Already at the design stage I account for code constraints, loading speed and maintenance cost. That's why the live website looks just like it did in Figma.

steps.title: Brief
steps.text: We discuss goals, audience, and examples you like and dislike. I gather everything that already exists: brand, copy, analytics.

steps.title: Prototype
steps.text: I show the structure and user flows without styling. We agree on the logic before anything gets drawn.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: I design the key screens, we approve the style, then I work through the remaining pages and responsive layouts.

steps.title: Handoff
steps.text: I deliver a Figma file with components and notes, answer the developers' questions — or build the website myself.

pricing.title: How much website design costs
pricing.note: The cost depends on the number of unique screens, the complexity of user flows and whether a design system is needed. I send an estimate after the brief.

plans.title: Website design
plans.text: Prototype, visual design and responsive layouts for a company or services website.

plans.title: Interface or app
plans.text: A client portal, web service or mobile app with a design system.

plans.title: Redesign
plans.text: A new look and logic for an existing website, keeping what already works.

plans.title: UX audit
plans.text: A review of user flows, errors and the places where leads are lost. You get a document with prioritised fixes.

items.question: What is UX/UI design in plain words?
items.answer: UX is the logic: what steps a person takes to get their task done and how easy that is. UI is the look: buttons, fonts, colours, icons. A good interface is both clear and pleasant — one doesn't work without the other.

items.question: How much does website design cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of unique screens and the complexity of user flows: a services website and a client portal with dozens of states are different jobs. The formats above give a rough guide; I give an exact estimate after the brief.

items.question: What's the difference between a prototype and a design?
items.answer: A prototype is a draft of the structure: blocks, copy and transitions, without colour or style. The design is the final look. We agree on the prototype first and then draw — that way changes cost less.

items.question: Which tool do you design in?
items.answer: Figma. You get access to the file: you can view it, leave comments and share it with colleagues via a link.

items.question: Can I order design only, without development?
items.answer: Yes. I'll hand the designs to your team with components and responsive rules and answer the developers' questions while they build.

items.question: Do you design logos and brand identities?
items.answer: Yes, when the website or product needs them. I've created logos and brand identities for QuantumTec, OcEx and VESTA.
